source_evidence: Institutional Shares (Class I) may have some of the lowest ongoing operating expenses, but there could be relatively high initial investment minimums and/or transaction fees to invest directly through a brokerage account.
question: Misconception: Class I shares are always available to every investor with no minimums or transaction fees. What is a more accurate view?
answer: Class I shares may have some of the lowest ongoing operating expenses, but they can have high initial investment minimums and/or transaction fees when purchased directly through a brokerage account. Some funds make them available to retail investors without a high minimum through options such as an employer retirement plan or an investment advisory account.
